facts.claim: Amsterdam's tourist tax (toeristenbelasting) is 12.5% of the overnight price excluding VAT, charged at hotels, hostels, guesthouses, B&Bs, apartments, short-stay rentals and campsites.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: 12.5% of the room price, excluding VAT
a third on top of the base rate

facts.claim: Amsterdam charges cruise operators a day tourist tax of €15 per passenger for day visits.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: a day tourist tax of €15 per passenger

facts.claim: From 1 January 2026 the Dutch VAT rate on short-stay accommodation in hotels, guesthouses and holiday businesses is 21% (previously 9%).

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: 21% of the room price (it was 9%)
VAT on a hotel room rose from 9% to 21%

facts.claim: Worked example (our arithmetic): a €200 room before VAT plus 21% VAT (€42) and 12.5% tourist tax (€25) costs €267 a night; three nights €801, of which €201 is tax.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: so the night costs €267
Three nights cost €801, of which €201 is tax

facts.claim: Trains run eight times an hour between Schiphol and Amsterdam Centraal, taking about 17 minutes; the station is directly below the terminal.

sources.title: Schiphol: Travelling from or to Amsterdam Schiphol airport by train

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: trains run eight times an hour to Amsterdam Centraal, in about 17 minutes

facts.claim: An NS single from Schiphol Airport to Amsterdam Centraal, second class, full fare, is €5.50 (NS journey planner, October 2026); single-use chip cards carry a €1.60 surcharge in 2026.

sources.title: NS journey planner (Schiphol Airport to Amsterdam Centraal, single, 2nd class, full fare: 550 cents)

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: gives €5.50 for a single in second class
adds a €1.60 surcharge

facts.claim: The Amsterdam Airport Express (line 397, Niteliner N97 at night) costs from €6.50 single and from €11.75 return; it departs every 10 minutes from stop B17 and stops at Museumplein, the Rijksmuseum and Leidseplein; drivers take debit or credit cards, not cash; OVpay accepted.

sources.title: Schiphol: Travelling to Schiphol airport by bus

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: A single costs from €6.50 and a return from €11.75
leaves every 10 minutes from stop B17

facts.claim: Schiphol's bus station is being renovated and some buses temporarily depart from and arrive at different locations.

sources.title: Schiphol: Travelling to Schiphol airport by bus

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: Schiphol's bus station is being renovated

facts.claim: The Amsterdam Travel Ticket costs €20 (1 day), €27 (2 days) and €34 (3 days) in 2026, with unlimited travel to and from Schiphol and throughout Amsterdam.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: €20 for one day, €27 for two and €34 for three in 2026

facts.claim: A GVB 1 hour ticket costs €3.40 in 2026.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: A GVB 1-hour ticket is €3.40

facts.claim: With OVpay (contactless debit/credit card, phone or OV-pas) GVB charges at most €10.50 per day for GVB trips; not valid on night buses or with the OV-chipkaart.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: at €10.50 (night buses excluded)

facts.claim: OVpay accepts contactless Maestro, V PAY, Mastercard and Visa cards and payment apps; check in and out with the same card; tickets cannot be bought on buses or on trams without a conductor.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: Pay by tapping a Maestro, V PAY, Mastercard or Visa card

facts.claim: A crossing with most GVB ferries is free for pedestrians and cyclists.

sources.title: GVB: the public transport company of Amsterdam

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: most GVB ferries are free for people on foot and on bikes

facts.claim: The Seventeenth-Century Canal Ring Area of Amsterdam inside the Singelgracht was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2010; it was built at the end of the 16th and beginning of the 17th centuries on drained swampland in concentric arcs.

sources.title: UNESCO: Seventeenth-Century Canal Ring Area of Amsterdam inside the Singelgracht

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage Site in 2010

facts.claim: ETIAS is not in operation and no applications are collected; the EU will announce the start date several months ahead; the fee will be EUR 20.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: ETIAS is not running yet
the fee will be €20

facts.claim: Pulitzer Amsterdam is a 5-star hotel in 25 restored 17th- and 18th-century canal houses at Prinsengracht 323; Cosy Rooms are its smallest.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: A five-star in 25 restored canal houses

facts.claim: Ambassade Hotel (Herengracht 341), open since 1953, has 56 rooms and suites across sixteen canal houses, and a Library Bar of more than 5,000 signed books.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: 56 rooms and suites across sixteen canal houses
more than 5,000 books

facts.claim: Mr. Jordaan (Bloemgracht 102) has single rooms of 11 m², doubles from 13 m² and twins of 15 m².

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: single rooms of 11 m², doubles from 13 m²

facts.claim: Linden Hotel (Lindengracht 251) is in a flatiron building; its doubles and twins are 11 to 14 m²; it takes no extra beds, groups over eight or more than three rooms.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: doubles and twins of 11 to 14 m²

facts.claim: Mandarin Oriental Conservatorium (Paulus Potterstraat 50) is in a late-19th-century former national savings bank and music conservatory; Stedelijk 1 min, Van Gogh Museum 2 min, Rijksmuseum 6 min on foot by the hotel's count.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: the Stedelijk is a minute away on foot, the Van Gogh Museum two and the Rijksmuseum six

facts.claim: Hotel Fita (Jan Luijkenstraat 37) has 21 rooms; twins 20 m², Superior Doubles 27 m²; breakfast €17.50 per person if not included; air conditioning only in some rooms.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: twins of 20 m² and Superior Doubles of 27 m²
breakfast is €17.50 a person

facts.claim: Hotel Okura Amsterdam occupies a 23-storey building on the outskirts of De Pijp, with four restaurants holding three Michelin stars between them.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: four restaurants holding three Michelin stars between them

facts.claim: Sir Albert (Albert Cuypstraat 2-6) is a former diamond factory; its gym is at Albert Cuypstraat 44.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: A former diamond factory on the Albert Cuypstraat

facts.claim: NH Collection Amsterdam Barbizon Palace (Prins Hendrikkade 59-72), opposite Centraal, has 268 rooms across 17th-century houses; all rooms include stairs.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: 268 rooms across a row of 17th-century houses

facts.claim: Hotel Sint Nicolaas (Spuistraat 1a) has a lift and 24-hour reception; doubles 21 m², twins 19 m²; no facilities for disabled guests; online check-in, rooms from 14:00.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: doubles of 21 m², twins of 19 m²

facts.claim: Sir Adam (Overhoeksplein 7) is in the 22-storey A'DAM Tower, a free three-minute ferry ride from Centraal.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: In the 22-storey A'DAM Tower

facts.claim: ClinkNOORD (Badhuiskade 3) is in a 1920s Art Deco laboratory; private en-suite rooms for 1 to 6, dorms of up to 14 beds; check-out by 10am.

articles/where-to-stay-in-amsterdam.html: dorms sleep up to 14, and check-out is by 10am
